messages:
maya-support: Customer reported duplicate outbound emails + invoice spike after a tool/function call failed then retried. Customer says: first call -> 502, client retried, then fallback to non-tool response executed and email sent twice. Customer PM is upset. Request IDs: r-98a7c3, r-98a7c3-retry

raj-eng: Can you paste the raw request/response headers and the request_id(s)? also which model and tool name?

maya-support: Model: gpt-4o-inference, tool: send_transactional_email. Attached headers from customer (redacted):

```
X-Request-Id: r-98a7c3
User-Agent: AcmeMailer/2.1
Authorization: Bearer ***
Idempotency-Key: none
```

Response sequence they reported: 2024-11-10T15:03:12Z -> 502 GatewayError (body: {"error":"tool_invoke_failed"})
2024-11-10T15:03:13Z -> client retried -> 200 OK fallback response (non-tool text) -> our system executed fallback path which also triggered send_transactional_email.

simon-oncall: Thanks. This looks like the transport-level retry raced with our fallback codepath. We recently changed fallback behavior to try a non-tool generation when the tool endpoint returns 5xx. If the client/library also retries at the same time, we can end up executing the tool call twice: first attempt that eventually completes, and the fallback attempt which triggers the side effect. We need logs from the gateway and tool runtime for r-98a7c3 and the retry id.

maya-support: Pasted a short excerpt from our gateway logs:

```
[15:03:12.112] gateway: incoming POST /v1/call-tool req=r-98a7c3
[15:03:12.345] runtime: tool_invoke START id=t-556 send_transactional_email
[15:03:12.789] runtime: tool_invoke ERROR id=t-556 exit=502 reason=upstream_timeout
[15:03:13.010] gateway: fallback_to_non_tool req=r-98a7c3 reason=tool_5xx
[15:03:13.213] runtime: tool_invoke COMPLETE id=t-556 status=200 side_effect=sent_email msg_id=msg-404
[15:03:13.220] billing: charge account=acct-442 token_units=37 invoice_line=inv-992
[15:03:13.401] runtime: fallback_generation COMPLETE req=r-98a7c3_fallback result=text
[15:03:13.410] runtime: fallback side_effect=sent_email msg_id=msg-405
[15:03:13.430] billing: charge account=acct-442 token_units=40 invoice_line=inv-993
```

raj-eng: This is the smoking gun — runtime completed the original tool_invoke after the gateway had already triggered fallback generation. That produced two sent_email side effects (msg-404 and msg-405) and two separate billing lines.

ella-billing: We've already seen the invoice spike for acct-442: +inv-992 and +inv-993 in a single session. Recommend issuing a credit for the duplicate line and flagging the account for manual review. I'll prepare a credit memo if eng confirms duplication was unintended.

jess-cs: I'll draft a customer message offering apology + credit and ask for permission to rotate any affected webhooks or keys. We should be careful not to admit code-level root cause before eng has confirmed the fix.

raj-eng: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Add idempotency-key requirement for tool calls that cause side effects (if missing, reject). 2) Ensure gateway waits for a tool_invoke ACK before deciding to fallback (return 202 ack quickly, then async status updates). 3) De-duplicate side effects in the runtime by checking tool invocation unique IDs (best-effort). Long term: enforce client-side idempotency header and opaque tool invocation tokens so retries are safe.

simon-oncall: I'll open an incident/bug: fallback-race-duplicate-sideeffects. Priority P1 for customer-impacting billing/side-effects. Temporary band-aid: set fallback disable for transactional tools (send_*/charge_*) until we patch.

maya-support: Customer asks for repro steps they can run to show the issue so they can validate the fix — what do we give them?

raj-eng: Provide a curl sequence: first, POST to /v1/call-tool with header `X-Request-Id: r-98a7c3-test` and no idempotency-key, then concurrently trigger a synthetic client retry (sleep 500ms then re-POST). I'll paste a simple repro script they can run in bash.

```
# repro: race retry -> fallback triggers duplicate
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/call-tool \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: r-98a7c3-test" \
  -d '{"tool":"send_transactional_email","args":{...}}' &
sleep 0.45
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/call-tool \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: r-98a7c3-test" \
  -d '{"tool":"send_transactional_email","args":{...}}'
```

Note: this deliberately omits Idempotency-Key to reproduce client-library retries.

ella-billing: Once eng confirms duplicate, I'll apply a credit and mark invoice lines as duplicate. Please tag me in the incident.

deploy-bot: Canary patch for "fallback-wait-ack" scheduled to roll to 10% at 2024-11-12T02:00:00Z (job id: canary-772).

simon-oncall: Action items: 1) eng to disable fallback for transactional tools immediately (raj). 2) eng to instrument runtime to emit tool_invoke ACK before heavy side-effects (raj + simon). 3) billing to prepare credit (ella). 4) cs to draft customer comms (jess). I'll coordinate postmortem once the incident is closed.

maya-support: Noted. I'll circle back to customer with interim update and estimated timeline. Thanks team. :pray:
